payload.summary: Build one exact candidate after source gates, carry producer identity to every consumer, and promote trusted main bytes only after CI completes successfully.
gates: Run the direct generated-version check before frozen script-disabled dependency installation. Complete Linux minimum/current source tests, lint, types and cheap tool checks before one explicit build and candidate pack; check tracked/untracked cleanliness around the build and require an absent package-artifacts directory.

Derive the tarball filename from the validated package version. Retain the atomic tarball/sidecar pair with size, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, integrity, source commit and relative path. Consumers download the original immutable producer artifact ID, verify its independently recorded SHA-256 and source metadata, restore only its reviewed dist files into an absent directory, and reuse strict package preflight without rebuilding or repacking.

Run the pinned published encephalon@0.3.0 oracle through schema 2 to 4 to 2, preserving public contracts and durable state. Every main candidate gets this proof; relevant production/public/persisted/package/release PR changes require it. Release labels, manual main runs and weekly main schedules force compatibility and historical release-tool regression. Unknown paths and failed selection cannot permit a skip.

Only a completed successful same-repository main CI run can promote the final verified pair through the code-free workflow_run copy. Bind trusted artifacts to source SHA, originating run and attempt. Cancelled/failed runs cannot promote, and consumer-only reruns reuse the original producer identity.

Before release, require current-main identity, Greptile 5/5, all selected gates and byte equality with the reviewed PR tarball. Record full digests and validate the exact tarball-only npm publish dry run.
payload.publication: Manual maintainer action only after final explicit approval: publish the reviewed tarball bytes. Agents never publish, rebuild for publication or publish a directory.
